candidate.objective: Act on suspected occult tendon injury even when gross movement and plain films are reassuring.
candidate.currentUpdate: The founder reviews {patientName}'s outside hand-wound record after a limited inspection attempt and bedside imaging.
candidate.task: Which disposition is best supported for {patientName}'s hand after this assessment?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Examination
items.value: The small palmar cut is accompanied by painful weak isolated finger flexion against resistance; active flexion remains possible.

items.label: Inspection attempt
items.value: Local anesthesia allowed inspection of the skin opening, but the deep flexor surface could not be fully seen.

items.label: Imaging record
items.value: Radiographs showed no fracture. The ultrasound report described continuity in the visualized tendon, but the segment beneath the wound was obscured by air and was not assessed.

choices.label: Splint and refer directly for hand-surgery assessment
choices.rationale: The negative observations do not cover the clinically suspicious segment. Protect the hand and obtain specialist assessment rather than use incomplete imaging as a referral gate.
choices.temptation: Interpret what each negative test actually assessed.
choices.counterfactual: Adequate visualization of the injured segment plus a complete painless normal examination could support a superficial-wound pathway.

choices.label: Splint and obtain repeat ultrasound before hand referral
choices.rationale: Repeat imaging can be a useful adjunct, but referral should not depend on a negative screen when clinical concern and incomplete exploration persist.
choices.temptation: Recognize the limited scan but make imaging clearance the prerequisite for specialist assessment.
choices.counterfactual: An adequately assessed low-risk injury with no unresolved tendon concern may be investigated without that same referral presumption.

choices.label: Splint and obtain MRI before hand referral
choices.rationale: Changing imaging modality does not remove the existing need for specialist assessment of a possible flexor laceration. The question is disposition, not a prohibition on adjunctive imaging.
choices.temptation: Seek a definitive-looking test before acting on unresolved clinical risk.
choices.counterfactual: MRI may be selected by the treating specialist when additional anatomical information will change management.

candidate.explanation: A report of continuity applies to the segment actually seen. Here the wound-level segment remains unassessed, the inspection was limited, and resisted function is abnormal. Splinting and prompt hand assessment remain appropriate. Ultrasound or MRI may add information; neither should be used to withhold referral until a lesion is demonstrated.

manualAuthorGate.coverTheKey: Every option protects the hand and starts a prompt assessment pathway. Routine delay and mobilization caricatures are removed. The report identifies the actual unassessed anatomy rather than asserting that all imaging is unreliable.
manualAuthorGate.sameDecisionStageAndCategory: Three protected hand-injury disposition pathways.
reasoningSteps: Recognize that the negative radiograph and partial ultrasound do not assess the clinically suspicious tendon segment.
Keep protection and specialist assessment in the disposition plan instead of making a repeat image the prerequisite for referral.
manualAuthorGate.closestError: Ordering prompt repeat ultrasound but using its result as a condition for hand referral.
manualAuthorGate.decidingObservation: Painful weak resisted flexion persists, and neither limited wound inspection nor the ultrasound visualized the wound-level tendon.
manualAuthorGate.counterfactual: A completely visualized superficial injury with normal painless isolated function could support routine wound care; an adequate specialist study can also guide treatment without being a prerequisite for initial assessment.
manualAuthorGate.deletionTest: Removing the limited segment changes how much reassurance the ultrasound provides. Removing abnormal loaded function reduces the reason to sustain concern despite gross movement.
manualAuthorGate.sequenceReview: Standalone clinic chart review. All earlier scored companions are removed. This node supplies the history it needs; no preceding feedback is visible.
manualAuthorGate.residentDifficulty: Moderate author prediction: deciding whether a limited negative study can gate referral is the intended competing error; re-review is pending.
manualAuthorGate.singleDefensibleBestAnswer: The stated observations distinguish the nearest competing action: Painful weak resisted flexion persists, and neither limited wound inspection nor the ultrasound visualized the wound-level tendon. Counterfactual re-solve: A completely visualized superficial injury with normal painless isolated function could support routine wound care; an adequate specialist study can also guide treatment without being a prerequisite for initial assessment.

The same repair attempt includes a final label scan: parallel length/category and removal of avoidable key-only noun matching.

candidate.objective: Separate active primary immunization from wound-specific passive protection using a fully established vaccine history.
candidate.currentUpdate: The founder reviews the wound and immunization entries from {patientName}'s outside ambulatory visit.
candidate.task: Which tetanus prophylaxis plan fits {patientName}'s recorded wound encounter?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Mechanism and depth
items.value: An indoor paper-trimmer blade produced a shallow linear skin cut. The assessment records no puncture tract, soil, saliva or devitalized tissue.

items.label: Vaccine history
items.value: The registry, previous records and patient agree that no tetanus-containing vaccine had ever been received before this encounter.

items.label: Other care
items.value: Cleansing and structural examination were completed.

choices.label: Start the vaccine primary series; no TIG
choices.rationale: The never-vaccinated history establishes an active-vaccine indication without an uncertain recent-dose interval. This clean minor wound does not call for TIG.
choices.temptation: Keep primary immunization and the wound-specific TIG decision separate.
choices.counterfactual: A soil-contaminated puncture in the same unvaccinated patient would call for both vaccine and TIG.

choices.label: Start the vaccine primary series and give TIG
choices.rationale: Active immunization is needed, but lack of previous vaccine does not by itself make TIG appropriate for this wound category.
choices.temptation: Apply the dirty-wound passive-protection rule to all unvaccinated patients.
choices.counterfactual: The same unvaccinated history with a dirty or major wound would support both.

choices.label: Give TIG; do not start the vaccine primary series
choices.rationale: This reverses the decisions: the record establishes a need for active immunization, while the wound does not establish a TIG indication.
choices.temptation: Use temporary antibody as a substitute for primary immunization.
choices.counterfactual: A dirty wound with HIV and a recently completed series can require TIG without another vaccine dose.

choices.label: Give neither vaccine nor TIG
choices.rationale: Low-risk wound status does not remove the independent primary-immunization need.
choices.temptation: Let the wound classification answer both prophylaxis questions.
choices.counterfactual: An appropriately immunized patient with a sufficiently recent dose can need neither product at a wound encounter.

candidate.explanation: Classify the wound from its mechanism and tissue findings, then check the vaccine history separately. This never-vaccinated patient needs active primary immunization. TIG is not indicated for the clean minor wound. Formulation and subsequent valid-dose scheduling remain part of the clinical vaccine plan.

manualAuthorGate.coverTheKey: The task does not name the wound category. Four balanced active/passive combinations prevent component frequency from selecting the answer. The vaccine history is decisive rather than a deliberately vague incomplete-series label.
manualAuthorGate.sameDecisionStageAndCategory: Four active/passive prophylaxis plans.
reasoningSteps: Classify the superficial unsoiled cut from the actual mechanism and tissue observations.
Start active primary immunization for a never-vaccinated person while withholding wound-inappropriate TIG.
manualAuthorGate.closestError: Giving both products merely because the patient has never been vaccinated.
manualAuthorGate.decidingObservation: A shallow unsoiled cut without devitalized tissue coexists with an established never-vaccinated history.
manualAuthorGate.counterfactual: A soil-contaminated puncture changes the passive-protection choice to vaccine plus TIG; a recent completed series changes the active-vaccine decision.
manualAuthorGate.deletionTest: Without tissue/exposure findings, the TIG branch is unresolved. Without the established never-vaccinated history, an immediate active dose could depend on prior valid-dose intervals.
manualAuthorGate.sequenceReview: Standalone clinic chart review. All earlier scored companions are removed. This node supplies the history it needs; no preceding feedback is visible.
manualAuthorGate.residentDifficulty: Fair moderate author prediction: two separate prophylaxis decisions at the same foundational level as the preserved tetanus PASS variants. No hard claim.
manualAuthorGate.singleDefensibleBestAnswer: The stated observations distinguish the nearest competing action: A shallow unsoiled cut without devitalized tissue coexists with an established never-vaccinated history. Counterfactual re-solve: A soil-contaminated puncture changes the passive-protection choice to vaccine plus TIG; a recent completed series changes the active-vaccine decision.
manualAuthorGate.repairAndRecheck: Replaced an undated incomplete series with an explicit never-vaccinated history, removing the dose-interval issue without inventing a schedule. Removed editorial source-dispute commentary from feedback.

candidate.objective: Apply the HIV TIG exception independently of a recent completed vaccine series.
candidate.currentUpdate: The founder reviews {patientName}'s outside wound record after a fence-wire puncture.
candidate.task: Which tetanus prophylaxis was indicated at {patientName}'s wound encounter?

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Wound
items.value: Soil was removed from a puncture wound during irrigation.

items.label: Vaccination record
items.value: The primary tetanus series was complete and the most recent tetanus-containing dose was two years before the injury.

items.label: Medical history
items.value: HIV infection is documented; the patient is receiving antiretroviral treatment.

choices.label: TIG; no tetanus-containing vaccine
choices.rationale: Current CDC guidance calls for TIG in a dirty wound with HIV regardless of prior immunization; the recent completed series does not require another vaccine dose.
choices.temptation: Apply the immune exception to passive protection while preserving the recent-dose vaccine rule.
choices.counterfactual: Without HIV or severe immunodeficiency, the same recent completed series could support neither product.

choices.label: Neither tetanus-containing vaccine nor TIG
choices.rationale: The recent completed series addresses the vaccine decision but does not override the HIV TIG exception.
choices.temptation: Stop the assessment once the vaccination record is reassuring.
choices.counterfactual: The same dirty wound with a recent completed series and no specified immune exception can need neither.

choices.label: Tetanus-containing vaccine and TIG
choices.rationale: HIV establishes a TIG indication here; it does not create a need to repeat a completed-series vaccine dose from two years earlier.
choices.temptation: Correctly add passive protection but also restart active protection without an indication.
choices.counterfactual: An incomplete series in this dirty wound would support both products.

choices.label: Tetanus-containing vaccine; no TIG
choices.rationale: This repeats an unnecessary vaccine while omitting the passive protection specifically indicated by the wound and HIV history.
choices.temptation: Treat immune status as a reason for an extra booster rather than check the actual TIG guidance.
choices.counterfactual: A completed series with a longer dirty-wound booster interval and no immune exception can call for vaccine without TIG.

candidate.explanation: Check the two prophylaxis decisions separately. HIV is a specified CDC exception requiring TIG for dirty/major wounds regardless of immunization history.
